requirements.requirement: Long-running background worker managed as a systemd service named inventory-worker
requirements.summary: Unit file /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service created with ExecStart running a persistent loop script; systemctl enable --now succeeded, status shows Active: running with child sleep process; is-enabled/is-active confirm managed, enabled state. Log ticks recorded every ~10s across multiple checks confirm continuous long-running behavior.

requirements.requirement: Confined so the service writes only inside /var/lib/inventory
requirements.summary: Service unit uses ProtectSystem=strict with ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory (plus ReadOnlyPaths for the script and other hardening). Directly tested: as the service user, a write to /etc/should-fail returned Permission denied (exit=1) while a write to /var/lib/inventory/should-work succeeded (exit=0). Test artifact was removed afterward.
Unit sets NoNewPrivileges=yes; directly confirmed by reading /proc/<MainPID>/status on the running process, which showed NoNewPrivs: 1.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol for node1 (independent of the task contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured (boot_id, uptime, active service, log ticks). Restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection. Boot identity changed (4a74...723 -> a886...051), corroborated by fixed before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots. Post-restart recovery directly observed: service re-enabled/active with new PID, and worker.log continued appending new ticks while preserving pre-restart entries.

overall_summary: The executor created a systemd-managed 'inventory-worker' service on node1 that runs continuously, writes only inside /var/lib/inventory (directly verified by a failed /etc write and a successful /var/lib/inventory write), and runs with NoNewPrivileges confirmed via /proc status. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and directly demonstrated: healthy pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity cross-checked against fixed snapshots, and confirmed post-restart recovery of both the service and its log data. Hygiene is high with only a trivial leftover /tmp/reboot.log file.
limitations: Confinement verification used the service's own MainPID and a manual sudo -u test rather than exhaustively probing every other filesystem path, so confinement outside /etc and /var/lib/inventory is inferred from the systemd sandboxing directives (ProtectSystem=strict) rather than directly tested against every location.

The node-restart evidence protocol was not part of the stated task contract but was independently assessed per instructions; its strong evidence does not add to core task functionality but does raise overall confidence in node health.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands were purposeful: user/directory creation, worker script and unit creation, service enablement, and a bounded write-confinement test whose artifact (/var/lib/inventory/should-work) was explicitly removed in the next command. The one minor residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a leftover redirect log from the backgrounded 'systemctl reboot' trigger command, which remains present in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot; it is small, non-sensitive, and a natural byproduct of the required restart-evidence step, but was not cleaned up. No failed or conflicting services, no unsafe network exposure, and no damaged package state were observed (failed-services and package-health snapshots unchanged and empty/healthy before and after).
